title: Don't include virtual sinks/sources in global mute behavior, either automatically or optionally
line: The speaker and microphone mute keys no longer mute virtual devices like Easy Effects sinks and sources, unless one is the default device.
explanation: Since global mute was introduced, the Mute and Mute Microphone shortcuts (and the applet's mute buttons, which invoke them) muted every sink and source the audio server reports, including virtual ones created by Easy Effects, loopbacks or routing setups. Those devices feed recordings, screen shares and OBS tracks, so pressing mute silenced much more than the speakers or microphone. The kded service now skips devices that pulseaudio-qt reports as virtual (no PA hardware flag; on PipeWire, node.virtual) unless the device is the current default, and a volume change on such a skipped device no longer cancels global mute. Unmuting still restores every device global mute had muted.

commits.message:
kded: leave virtual devices alone when muting globally

The speaker and microphone mute shortcuts muted every device, including
virtual ones used for effects and routing, silencing recordings and
streams. Now virtual devices are only muted when they are the default.

BUG: 508170

media.caption: Master: after pressing Mute and Mute Microphone, the virtual Easy_Effects_Sink and Easy_Effects_Source are muted along with Speakers and Microphone.
With the fix: the same keys mute Speakers and Microphone, the virtual Easy Effects devices keep playing and recording.

reviews.text: This cleanly implements the consensus from the bug report in plasma-pa's AudioShortcutsService by excluding virtual sinks and sources from global mute unless the virtual device is currently the default device. Keeping the default device included ensures pressing mute always silences active output/input and keeps the applet mute indicator in sync when Easy Effects or a network sink is set as default, while unmuting still restores any device that global mute previously muted. Ignoring volume and unmute events on skipped virtual devices also avoids accidentally breaking global mute.

Does what Nate settled on in comments 1 and 3: global mute in plasma-pa's kded now skips devices pulseaudio-qt reports as virtual (the same flag behind the applet's 'Show virtual devices'), keeps muting the default device even if virtual, and a volume or unmute change on a skipped device no longer cancels global mute. The unmute path is list-based, so skipped devices are never touched, and the change fits cleanly into applyGlobalSinkMute/applyGlobalSourceMute. The before/after dumps and KCM screenshots prove it, and the default-is-virtual and hardware-volume regressions were checked; comment 4's default-only request is a separate bug (435199). Minor nit: if a virtual device becomes the default while global mute is already on, it stays unmuted, because only port changes re-apply mute. Audio is still silent through the muted hardware underneath, but the applet's mute state may not match until the key is pressed again.
